Since \(a_{n+1}^2-a_n^2=4\) and \(a_1^2=4\), we get
\[
a_n^2=4n \implies a_n=2\sqrt n.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{1}{a_{k+1}+a_k}=\frac{1}{2(\sqrt{k+1}+\sqrt k)}=\frac{\sqrt{k+1}-\sqrt k}{2}.
\]
So
\[
\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{1}{a_{k+1}+a_k}
=\frac12\sum_{k=1}^n(\sqrt{k+1}-\sqrt k)
=\frac{\sqrt{n+1}-1}{2}.
\]
Set equal to \(5\):
\[
\frac{\sqrt{n+1}-1}{2}=5
\implies \sqrt{n+1}=11
\implies n+1=121
\implies n=120.
\]

\[
\boxed{120}
\]
